Patient Narrative: Subject 1001-0023

Marta Kowalczyk (initials M.K.), a 64-year-old woman born 14-Mar-1961, MRN 00482913, was randomized on 02-Jun-2025 (randomization no. R-58213) and received her first dose the same day. She lives at 418 Alder Crest Road, Linden Valley, OR 97411 and can be reached at (555) 014-2290.

On 16-Jun-2025 she reported a grade 2 headache and nausea. Ms. Kowalczyk was seen at the clinic by the investigator, Dr. Samuel Okafor, who judged the event possibly related to study drug. Treatment was not interrupted. The event resolved on 19-Jun-2025 without sequelae. Her medical history includes hypertension, controlled with lisinopril.

5.2 Exclusion Criteria

Participants are not eligible for enrollment if any of the following apply:

1. Known hypersensitivity to the investigational product or any of its excipients.
2. Estimated glomerular filtration rate below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 at screening.
3. Active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection, or known HIV infection with a detectable viral load.
4. Participation in another interventional clinical study within 30 days before the first dose.
5. Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or unwillingness to use highly effective contraception during the treatment period and for 90 days after the last dose.
6. Any condition that, in the judgment of the investigator, would interfere with the evaluation of the study objectives or put the participant at undue risk.

Participants who fail screening may be rescreened once, after approval from the medical monitor. All screening assessments must then be repeated.

Monitoring Visit Report: Interim Monitoring Visit 6, Linden Valley Medical Center

Monitor: Tom Becker, Clinical Research Associate
Site staff present: Dr. Samuel Okafor (Principal Investigator), Lena Brandt (Study Coordinator)

1. Overview

The visit covered source data verification for the three subjects enrolled since the previous visit, a review of the investigator site file, investigational product accountability, and follow-up of the action items raised at visit 5. All action items from visit 5 were closed except the outstanding training record for the new pharmacy technician.

2. Investigator Site File

The investigator site file was complete and current. The latest protocol amendment and the revised informed consent form were filed with the ethics committee approval letter. The delegation log was updated to add the new pharmacy technician.

3. Source Data Verification

Source data verification was completed for all visits through visit 4. Two findings were raised. First, a concomitant medication recorded in the clinic notes was missing from the electronic case report form; the coordinator entered it during the visit. Second, the source documents for one subject listed an outdated contact address. The coordinator confirmed that the current address is 2207 Quarry Hill Lane, Apartment 5B, Linden Valley, OR, updated the source, and noted the change in the subject file. No other discrepancies were found.

4. Investigational Product

Drug accountability was reconciled for all dispensed kits. Returned tablets were counted and matched the dosing diaries. No temperature excursions were reported.

5. Action Items

The site will file the pharmacy technician training record and send confirmation to the monitor before the next visit.

9.4 Statistical Methods: Protocol FTX-4471-012 (NCT09990421; EudraCT 2031-004417-22), Version 4.0, effective 03-Feb-2025

Time-to-event endpoints will be estimated with the Kaplan-Meier method and compared with a stratified log-rank test. Creatinine clearance is calculated with the Cockcroft-Gault formula. Secondary continuous endpoints are compared with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, with Bonferroni correction across the four secondary endpoints.

Investigational product FTX-4471 is supplied as 50 mg tablets, lot LT-240917-B, in kits numbered from K-004417. Dosing visits occur on Day 1 and Day 15 ±2. Database lock is planned for 30-Nov-2026.

Patientennarrativ: Prüfungsteilnehmer 2104-0012

Jürgen Hoffmeister (geb. 07.11.1949), wohnhaft Lindenweg 12, Neuwaldstadt, wurde am 12.05.2025 in die Studie aufgenommen. Am 03.07.2025 (Tag 53) entwickelte er eine Pneumonie und wurde stationär im Klinikum Neuwaldstadt aufgenommen.

Die Prüfärztin, Dr. med. Katrin Albers, bewertete das Ereignis als schwerwiegend und nicht mit der Prüfmedikation in Zusammenhang stehend. Die Behandlung mit der Prüfmedikation wurde fortgesetzt. Herr Hoffmeister wurde nach neun Tagen entlassen; das Ereignis gilt als abgeklungen.
